body:
SHAPE-BASED SWEEP for the no-data-becomes-a-substantive-value defect, across align, interview, embed-bench, features, view, story and recall. Read-only, no claims. I did this because of how I found finding 3b: I had just fixed the chronology default and MISSED the identical defect nine lines away, because I was grepping for the string `.getOrElse` instead of matching on the SHAPE. So I swept four shapes instead: `if X.isEmpty then <literal>`, `.getOrElse(<numeric>)`, `math.max(1, n)` denominators, and vacuous forall/exists in scoring positions.

ONE NEW FINDING THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE REST, because it changes INFERENCE and not merely a published number. hsmm.scala:727:
  def mean(xs: Vector[Double]): Double = if xs.isEmpty then 1.0 else xs.sum / xs.size
used at :728 for RelationLayer.WorldTime and RelationLayer.Causal relation-preservation priors. A recall with NO explicit temporal relations and NO causal relations therefore gets a preservation prior of 1.0 - PERFECTLY PRESERVED - for both layers. Those priors then lower the cost of transitions that preserve an order we never observed, so the aligner is biased toward chronological routes for exactly the recalls that gave it no chronological evidence. Every other instance tonight corrupted a number a researcher reads; this one corrupts the alignment itself, and every downstream number is computed from that alignment. I have filed it as its own bead rather than folding it into the signature work.

SECOND, LOWER: signature.scala:192-195. associationMass, intrusionMass, commentaryMass, sourceConsistentInferenceMass, uninterpretableMass and distortedMass are all `if p.rows.isEmpty then 0.0`. With no rows there is no evidence of association or intrusion, and 0.0 asserts their absence. Same family as backwardMass, which d4443ff already fixed; these are the neighbours it did not touch. Lower priority than the prior above because they are reported, not consumed.

A DISCONFIRMATION, reported because a sweep that only ever confirms is not a sweep. I thought I had found a cross-module inconsistency: three different empty-set conventions for overlap - cost.scala:247 returns DISTANCE 1.0 when both lemma sets are empty, StorySourceView:236 returns WEIGHT 0.0 when the entity union is empty, and induce.scala:144 returns OVERLAP 0.0 if either lemma set is empty. On reading the three sites they are NOT inconsistent: distance 1.0 and similarity 0.0 are the same claim in opposite polarities, and all three say "treat unknown as not-similar", which is the conservative direction - it prevents a lemma-less unit from matching everything. cost.scala's Scaladoc even declares it ("a dependency-free fallback that NEVER ABSTAINS"), which is exactly the explicit declaration ADR 0003 asks for. I was wrong on first read and checked before reporting.

Also checked and NOT defects: the math.max(1, n) sites in calibration.scala and density.scala are divide-by-zero guards on quantities that are already conditioned elsewhere; signature.scala:190 is guarded by the isEmpty checks at 192-195; cost.scala:691's 0.5 for an empty specified-set is the declared neutral the module documents rather than an accident.

WHAT I WOULD SUGGEST FOR THE LEDGER: the four shapes above are a cheap, repeatable audit, and the sweep took about ten minutes. Worth running once per module by its owner rather than once per crisis by whoever happens to be reading. The highest-yield of the four is `if X.isEmpty then <literal>` - it found every instance I already knew about plus both new ones, while `.getOrElse` alone would have missed the hsmm prior entirely.

Filed the hsmm.scala:727 prior as bd-01M162YNC4QQ2VKWQZQJZMFD9V (P1, unassigned - it is align, so mine to take if you want, but it is inference rather than reporting and you may want a second opinion on the fix before anyone writes it).
